newsitem.title: USA: CBOT corn ends higher as rains drench Ohio crops.
newsitem.headline: CBOT corn ends higher as rains drench Ohio crops.

text.p: CBOT corn futures closed higher, boosted by some concern about the impact on crops of heavy rains in Ohio and indications the market had become oversold after recent weakness, dealers said.
"There are parts of Ohio which really got doused and that gave the market a boost. I think though it is a relatively small area," said Everen Securities analyst Joel Karlin.

Weather Services Corp reported that between 1.50 and 3.00 inches of rain fell in Ohio and in parts of Indiana and Kentucky over the weekend, sparking talk that newly-emerged corn and soybean crops could be washed out.
Dealers said it may be too late to replant corn.
Sentiment also continued to be buoyed by Friday's bullish weekly U.S. Department of Agriculture export sales report.
"Demand (for corn) has not been too bad," Karlin said, noting Friday's report appeared to have had a greater market impact on Monday than it did on Friday.
USDA on Friday said U.S. net export sales of corn during the week ended May 22 totalled 1,002,900 tonnes, well above expectations for 400,000 to 500,000 tonnes.
July corn ended 3-1/4 cents a bushel higher at $2.74 a bushel with other months up 3-1/2 to 4-1/2 cents.

Dealers noted USDA reported corn export inspections, for the week to May 29, totalled 27.34 million bushels, up from 22.37 million a week earlier. The total was much as expected with trade estimates ranging from 25 to 30 million.

Pit sources said featured buyers of corn included FCC (2.0 million bushels December, 1.5 million July) and LIT (2.0 million December) while Cargill Investor Services was among noted sellers (2.0 million December, 1.0 million September).
Corn futures volume was estimated by the CBOT at 49,000 contracts, versus 47,709 traded Friday.
